item.research_question: Can a simple YBCO superconductor formulation with Y2O3 nanoparticles be used to produce high-performance 2G HTS wires for fusion applications?
item.processing_route: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD) on a Hastelloy C276 substrate with a buffer layer architecture based on MgO textured using ion beam assisted deposition
item.test_conditions: Measurements at 4.2 K and 20 K in magnetic fields up to 20 T and 31.2 T
key_findings: Record engineering current density of over 1000 A/mm2 at 20 K, 20 T
Record engineering current density of over 2000 A/mm2 at 4.2 K, 20 T
High critical current values in the 220-270 A/4 mm range at 20 K, 20 T
High critical current values in the 450-570 A/4 mm range at 4.2 K, 20 T
Low statistical scatter in the ratio of the Ic at 4.2 and 20 K to that at 77 K in self-field
YBCO wire outperforms GdBCO wire by a factor of 1.5 to over 2.5 in the entire range of magnetic fields studied at temperatures of 65 K and below
item.mechanism: The Y2O3 nanoparticles provide isotropic pinning amplified by point defects arising from the epitaxial strain induced by the presence of the nanoparticles, and the high CuO2 plane hole doping level minimises the electronic anisotropy and strengthens the vortex pinning of YBCO
item.future_work: Investigation of the effects of the size, concentration and orientation type of the nanoparticles on the pinning properties of YBCO
quotes: We have established a record engineering current density in commercial wire of over 1000 A/mm2 at 20 K, 20 T and over 2000 A/mm2 at 4.2 K, 20 T

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a simple YBCO superconductor formulation with Y2O3 nanoparticles be used to produce high-performance 2G HTS wires for fusion applications?. System: YBa2Cu3O7 (YBCO) with Y2O3 nanoparticles. Processing: Pulsed laser deposition (PLD) on a Hastelloy C276 substrate with a buffer layer architecture based on MgO textured using ion beam assisted deposition. Test conditions: Measurements at 4.2 K and 20 K in magnetic fields up to 20 T and 31.2 T. Findings: Record engineering current density of over 1000 A/mm2 at 20 K, 20 T; Record engineering current density of over 2000 A/mm2 at 4.2 K, 20 T; High critical current values in the 220-270 A/4 mm range at 20 K, 20 T; High critical current values in the 450-570 A/4 mm range at 4.2 K, 20 T; Low statistical scatter in the ratio of the Ic at 4.2 and 20 K to that at 77 K in self-field; YBCO wire outperforms GdBCO wire by a factor of 1.5 to over 2.5 in the entire range of magnetic fields studied at temperatures of 65 K and below. Mechanism: The Y2O3 nanoparticles provide isotropic pinning amplified by point defects arising from the epitaxial strain induced by the presence of the nanoparticles, and the high CuO2 plane hole doping level minimises the electronic anisotropy and strengthens the vortex pinning of YBCO. Future work: Investigation of the effects of the size, concentration and orientation type of the nanoparticles on the pinning properties of YBCO. Quote: "We have established a record engineering current density in commercial wire of over 1000 A/mm2 at 20 K, 20 T and over 2000 A/mm2 at 4.2 K, 20 T"
